syllabus.scope: Chemistry Unit 1 Some Basic Concepts: mole concept, molar mass, percentage composition, empirical and molecular formulae, stoichiometry; Unit 5 Solutions: concentration in mass percentage and mole fraction.

corpus.coverageNotes: Targeted scan of five April 2026 papers, 375 questions available. Not all shifts, exhaustive topic classification or a five-year weightage analysis.

priority.rationale: Two verified relevant questions in the targeted five-paper April 2026 corpus. Chosen for a common prerequisite misconception and a short visual explanation, not an invented chapter-weightage claim.

pyqs.independentSolution: 100 g solution contains 10 g urea and 90 g water. Urea CO(NH2)2 has molar mass 60 g/mol, water 18 g/mol. Amounts are 1/6 mol and 5 mol. Water mole fraction 5/(5+1/6)=30/31. To three decimal places this rounds to 0.968, not 0.967; the official option 0.967 is the closest listed value, which is explicitly noted.

C:H mass ratio 12:1 gives atom/mole ratio 12/12:1/1=1:1. Two carbon atoms mean C2H2, molar mass 26. 3.38/26=0.13 mol hydrocarbon yields 0.26 mol CO2, hence 0.26×44=11.44 g. Cross-check: carbon mass 3.38×12/13=3.12 g -> 0.26 mol C -> 0.26 mol CO2.

targetQuestionText: A solution contains 10% urea by mass in water. What is the mole fraction of water? Use molar masses of 60 g/mol for urea and 18 g/mol for water.
verificationNotes: Original official question-page images inspected; exact final-key IDs matched. Solutions calculated independently and numerical cases checked. Explicit assumptions and option rounding caveats recorded in each question.
